summary: Notre Dame returns from its bye after the 28-24 loss at BYU. Clock operation and ball security remain lessons from that game; Greathouse’s receiving role carries into Saturday’s noon ET meeting with Navy.

items.headline: Notre Dame meets Navy at noon ET on ABC
items.tldr: Saturday’s neutral-site game is at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough. Plan for the Massachusetts venue and the early Eastern television window.

items.headline: Greathouse earns a comeback player of the week honor
items.tldr: He caught eight passes for 125 yards at BYU. Watch how his routes give the offense an answer when the defense closes the first throwing lane.

items.headline: Big 12 acknowledges a replay error in the BYU finish
items.tldr: The conference said one second should have remained after the final play. The October 17 result still stands; keep the officiating correction separate from a changed outcome.

items.headline: A failed spike costs Notre Dame a first-half chance
items.tldr: Irish Sports Daily recounts Carr’s fumble before halftime at BYU. Watch the exchange and clock operation before asking the offense to manufacture another late scoring chance.

items.headline: Notre Dame resumes after a 28-24 loss at BYU
items.tldr: The Irish had an open date October 24. Use the next game to judge the response on the field rather than assuming the extra practice has resolved the close-game errors.

lead.headline: Make the next possession count.
lead.body: Get the snap, timing and first read settled before chasing extra yards. Defend Navy with clear run assignments and coverage that remains intact when the formation invites the secondary forward.

matchup.thesis: Stay disciplined through the whole down
matchup.question: What should fans watch in the next game?
matchup.answer: On offense, make the receiving outlet and protection work together. On defense, identify the ball carrier without abandoning the deeper assignment before the play declares itself.

signals.title: Clock operation
signals.summary: Secure the snap before the next decision
signals.detail: Know the clock, down and intended finish before the exchange. Give a hurry-up possession a practiced operation rather than a series of improvised reactions.
signals.prompt: What should I watch for with clock operation?

signals.title: Receiving options
signals.summary: Give the quarterback a clean outlet
signals.detail: Watch the release against contact and the space between routes. A dependable inside completion can keep the quarterback from holding the ball into pressure.
signals.prompt: What should I watch for with receiving options?

signals.title: Run assignments
signals.detail: Identify the ball before pursuing across the formation. Keep the edge and inside fits connected so one wrong step does not open a second lane.
signals.prompt: What should I watch for with run assignments?

signals.title: Coverage patience
signals.summary: Carry the route behind run action
signals.detail: Keep eyes and leverage on the receiver until the assignment changes. Do not let the urge to join a tackle leave the deeper throw undefended.
signals.prompt: What should I watch for with coverage patience?

nextGameNote: Watch defensive eyes and assignments through Navy’s run action. On offense, make the snap and clock operation as dependable as the receiving plan.
